package_info.package_versions: Versions with known vulnerabilities exploited in Equifax and other breaches (e.g., CVE-2017-5638 and others)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contained a known, unpatched security vulnerability that allowed remote code execution. Attackers exploited this vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to sensitive systems, demonstrating that the presence of such vulnerabilities in widely used open source components can be weaponized for large-scale breaches.

execution_context.file_location: Struts core library (vulnerable class handling file upload requests)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The vulnerable code in Apache Struts allowed attackers to inject malicious OGNL (Object-Graph Navigation Language) expressions via crafted HTTP headers, which were then evaluated by the framework, leading to arbitrary code execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code evaluates user-supplied OGNL expressions from HTTP headers, which can result in arbitrary command execution on the server, enabling remote code execution and system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evaluating user-supplied expressions or code is inherently dangerous and enables attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly validate and sanitize user input, never evaluating it as code. The actual behavior allowed direct code execution from untrusted input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Templating engines or scripting interfaces may evaluate expressions, but only from trusted sources and with strict sandboxing.
key_indicators: Ability to execute arbitrary system commands

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with malicious OGNL payload in headers.
attack_chain.leads_to: OGNL payload is evaluated by the vulnerable Struts component.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable Struts code evaluates the OGNL expression, resulting in arbitrary code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access to the server, enabling data theft or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Evaluation of user-supplied OGNL or similar expressions at runtime
Unexpected process execution triggered by HTTP request headers
Unusual outbound network connections from application servers
file_indicators: Struts core libraries with known vulnerable versions
Application logs showing OGNL errors or stack traces
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with suspicious OGNL payloads in headers
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure following exploitation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for OGNL-related errors or stack traces, inspect HTTP request headers for suspicious payloads, and flag any process execution or network activity initiated by the application server that is not part of normal operations. Use software composition analysis tools to identify and block deployment of known vulnerable Struts versions.
